purpose: The fixed page list the scheduled Notice performance probe visits. The list is committed so that every synthetic observation comes from the same pages under the same profile, and so a change to what is measured is a reviewed change rather than a drifting sample.
selection_rationale: Eight Notice documents chosen to spread the client work a Notice page can carry rather than to represent what residents read. The spread covers both published notice kinds (award and solicitation) and the four client owners that dominate a Notice page's readiness: a land-use meeting agenda, a rule text, an attachment table, and procurement context enrichment. Two anchors bound the range: the heaviest and the lightest document measured on the list. Popularity is deliberately not a selection input, because an equal-visit probe carries no popularity weighting and must not be read as though it did.
maintenance: Publisher windows roll, so a listed notice can stop resolving. The probe reports an unreachable page per slot instead of failing the run, and a page that has been unreachable across consecutive slots is replaced by a reviewed edit to this file. The probe never substitutes a page of its own.
document_bytes_note: Measured response bytes for the served document on the date above. A single measured observation for the size spread, not a budget and not a latency claim.

device_profile.rationale: A mid-range phone viewport. The readiness budget is set for slow devices, so the probe measures the harder profile rather than a desktop one.

network_profile.rationale: A fixed throttle so a change in the measured distribution is a change in the deployed surface rather than a change in the network the probe happened to get.

visit_policy.rationale: One cold visit per page per slot. A repeat visit inside a slot would measure a warm cache and a warm connection, which is a different question, and a shared browser context would carry state between pages.

pages.rationale: A subcommittee meeting notice carrying an agenda of land-use items. The largest document on the list and the one with the most client-rendered rows.
An emergency rule amendment. Exercises the rule-text owner, which is deferred and must never gate primary readiness.
An award notice with structured attachment tables. Exercises the attachment-metadata owner.
The one notice with precomputed related-attachment edges, so the related-document path is measured on at least one page per slot.
A solicitation already loaded by the controlled generator, so the synthetic group and the lab group share at least one page and a difference between them is not a difference in what was visited.
A current solicitation inside the resident procurement window, so the procurement-context enrichment owner has data to render.
A public hearing notice. The third published section on the list, so the spread is not two kinds wide.
A short public meeting notice. The smallest document on the list and the lower bound of the size spread.
